messages.author: 0bbc509a820bf122
messages.subject: Importing maps to INLA
parts:
I am new to INLA program but want to use it for spatio-temporal modeling of disease incidence of humans. INLA appears useful as it reduce time to process and gives similar estimates obtained using WINBUGS. However, I found seen worked or practical examples in the INLA-R program manual how to import or attach users maps that are not built-in the library. To link model outputs for space-time risk-maps. Are there simplified methods or examples with this regard?
Asnakew

Hi

There is no tools to attach usersmaps. I think that some of the tools
that you use to handle these maps also have tools to extract the
adjancy matrix, which I think you ask for. (perhaps you mean to import
data and other info????) From that one, its shouldn't be difficult to
write the graph-file required.

> inla.graph.convert.2
function (adj, num, graph.file = "graph.txt", c.indexing = FALSE)
{

convert from `adjancy and num', as required by WinBugs to the
inla-format. as you see, the conversion is quite easy.


so the main issue is to extract the adjancy file from the map.


if I missed your point, let me know.
